question: Can dropout, normally a regulariser against overfitting, reduce underfitting if applied only early in training, and can the mirror (late dropout) reduce overfitting?
hypothesis: Early in training dropout lowers mini-batch gradient direction variance and error against the whole-dataset gradient, so switching it on early (then off) helps underfitting models fit better.
contributions: Analysis showing dropout reduces gradient direction variance and error early in training (GDV and GDE metrics)
Evaluation on ImageNet-1K and downstream tasks

method.summary: Train vision models on ImageNet-1K with dropout or stochastic depth active only for the first epochs (early) or only after the first epochs (late), compared with no dropout and standard dropout at 0.1. Gradient direction variance and error are measured on ViT-T/16 to explain the effect.
method.task: ImageNet-1K image classification, plus fine-tuning on COCO, ADE20K and five classification sets

datasets.name: CIFAR-100, Flowers, Pets, STL-10, Food-101
datasets.split: fine-tuning per MoCo v3 and SLIP settings

models.name: ViT-T/16
models.params: inferred: 5-20M range (paper gives a range for small models)

models.name: Mixer-S/32, ConvNeXt-Femto, Swin-F
models.architecture: MLP-Mixer, ConvNeXt, Swin Transformer small variants

models.name: ViT-B and Mixer-B
models.architecture: overfitting-regime models, trained with late s.d.

other.note: paper text says ViT-B and Mixer-B have 59M and 86M respectively

training.objective: inferred: cross-entropy classification with label smoothing 0.1
training.dropout: 0.0 baseline; early dropout rate 0.1-0.7 by model (Table 9), 50 epochs, linear decreasing to 0; standard comparison 0.1
training.regularisation: randaugment (9, 0.5), mixup 0.8, cutmix 1.0, random erasing 0.25, label smoothing 0.1, layer scale 1e-6, gradient clip None, EMA None; improved recipe mixup and cutmix 0.3

other.late_sd: no s.d. for first 50 epochs then constant rate (ViT-B 0.4, Mixer-B 0.2)
other.constant_early_dropout: best at 20 epochs rather than 50 (Appendix D)

metrics.name: GDV
metrics.definition: average pairwise cosine distance among mini-batch gradients

metrics.name: GDE
metrics.definition: average cosine distance of mini-batch gradients to whole-dataset gradient; Table 1 reports AUC over first 1500 iterations

baselines: linear increasing, decreasing, curriculum (Morerio 2017), annealed (Rennie 2014) schedules
eval.protocol: 3 seeds, mean reported; drop rate and epochs lightly swept per model

limits: Only supervised vision tasks; self-supervised pre-training and NLP untested (Appendix G).
Interaction with training duration and optimizer not explored (Appendix G).
Why training loss only falls after dropout ends is unexplained; authors suggest a better local optimum.
Gains are small (0.2 to 0.9 points) compared with seed std ~0.14%.
Late s.d. found no improvement on ConvNeXt-B and Swin-B.
Early dropout is rate-sensitive for dropout (not s.d.) and fails for ViT-B.
The regime (under/overfit) is defined operationally: better with standard dropout means overfitting.
